newsitem.title: COMOROS: Moslem leader in Comoros attacks "obscene" attire.
newsitem.headline: Moslem leader in Comoros attacks "obscene" attire.

text.p: The spiritual leader of Moslems on the Comoro Islands has marked the holy fasting month of Ramadan with a call for a crackdown on women wearing "obscene clothes".
"Their behaviour is deeply corrupting our society," Said Mohamed Charif told the 600,000 islanders in a weekend radio broadcast.
He told security forces to "redouble their efforts to track down ladies and girls wearing obscene clothes whose number has been unceasingly increasing".
Charif is chairman of the council of Ulemas or senior Islamic jurists and theologians. He did not specify the type of clothes that irked him.
But some women islanders favour Western fashions, including miniskirts, perhaps influenced by the foreign tourists who flock to the Comoros because of the beautiful beaches.

The Indian Ocean islands, whose population is almost entirely Moslem, began fasting on Saturday. The Islamist party won three of the 43 seats in parliament in last December's general elections boycotted by the opposition.

Charif's address was in place of the usual presidential message to the nation on the eve of Ramadan. There was no explanation for President Mohamed Taki's decision not to make the broadcast in person.

This year's fasting month will be a sombre one for many islanders because civil servants, the majority of the salaried workforce, have not been paid for 10 months and cannot afford the usual feasts which traditionally end each day's fast.
Daily cuts in electricity and water supplies are also becoming frequent.
